absent: Concurrency and locking rules for mapping iterators, scatter tables, pools, splitter outputs, and sequential buffers beyond xarray RCU protection are not shown.
Initialization, reset, and teardown semantics for mapping iterators and sequential buffers including overflow clearing are not shown.
Non chained scatter table allocation, release, and DMA mapping lifecycle details are not shown.
Detailed binary format argument encoding, alignment, and pointer extension semantics beyond dispatch categories are not shown.
Error handling for path lookup and mangling failures beyond negative result propagation is not shown.
Caller contexts allowed for atomic versus local versus general mapping selection are not shown.
Memory layout of scatter entries, tables, folio queues, and iterator structures is not shown.

findings.text: Scatter list mapping iterator advance that closes any current mapping, moves to the next page segment when required, exposes the current page with its usable address and length under the caller selected mapping flavor, and reports exhaustion when no further page remains.

Bidirectional transfer helpers between a linear buffer and a scatter list with optional leading skip, where direction selects reading from or writing to the list, iteration uses local mapping, total progress is bounded by caller length, and the result is the byte count actually moved with zero when skip cannot be satisfied.

Scatter list range clearing helper defined by skip and length that walks the affected segments with local writable mapping, writes zeros bounded by remaining length, and returns the count cleared with zero when skip exceeds available data.

Top level extraction entry that rejects zero size or zero entry budgets with empty result, routes user, block vector, kernel vector, folio queue, and xarray iterators to dedicated handlers, and warns while reporting an input output failure for unsupported iterator kinds.

Extraction handlers append new entries at the current table end, grow the table count per emitted segment, consume from remaining byte and entry allowances, respect the starting offset inside the source, and update source position on success.
Xarray backed extraction acquires read side RCU protection for the duration of the folio lookup walk and releases it before updating the iterator and returning.
Chained chunk pool descriptor that associates an entry capacity with a name plus a slab cache handle and a mempool handle used for scatter list chunk allocation.

Split planning record that links the first input entry of a span with the span entry count, the byte offset skipped in the first entry, the valid length kept in the last entry, and the destination span pointer.

Pool sizing facts where each pool keeps a reserve depth of two, base capacities cover eight and sixteen with conditional larger powers plus the configured chunk size, pool count equals the descriptor table length, and chunk sizes above two hundred fifty six fail the build.
Sequential buffer hex encoding uses a maximum input chunk of eight bytes with an output staging capacity sized for two characters per byte plus a trailing separator.

Mapping iterator usage progresses from start through optional skip into repeated advance and access steps finished by stop, where advance ending the list terminates iteration and stop always releases the active mapping.
Sequential buffer appends stay writable while room remains and latch into overflow on shortage, thereafter reporting failure until a reset performed outside these fragments.

Append admissibility requires current content length plus requested length to fit within total capacity, while string append reserves room for termination without charging that byte against content length.

Bounded sequential buffer insertion interfaces for text, single bytes, raw memory, endian sensitive hex words, and binary encoded formatted output, each signaling success or overflow and treating zero total size as a programming warning.

Sequential buffer output interfaces deliver used content to a sequence file, to the kernel log split by lines with level prefixing, to user memory from an offset with busy and fault reporting, as row oriented hex dumps with address offset or plain prefixes and a default row width, and as a mangled path with committed length.

Binary argument format renderer that decodes literal text plus width, precision, character, string, pointer, percent, and numeric directives into a bounded destination, guarantees termination when size is positive, and returns generated length excluding terminator limited to the positive range.
Destination sizes beyond the positive signed range trigger a one time warning and produce empty output, and generated lengths beyond that range are clamped with a warning.
Failed user page extraction releases every page pinned beyond the original table length by unpinning in reverse order before propagating the failure status.
Chunk length to pool choice sends counts of eight or fewer to the first pool and maps larger counts by binary order offset, requiring the count to stay within the maximum chunk size.

Chained table allocation reuses a caller supplied first chunk when it already covers the request, otherwise allocates chained chunks from pools in atomic context while treating first chunk sizes of zero or one as absent, and frees any chained remainder if allocation fails.
Early pool setup creates a slab cache and a slab backed mempool for every size class with error logging, and on any failure tears down all pools and caches before reporting memory exhaustion.

Scatter list splitting first plans spans by validating requested sizes against available input while honoring initial skip and physical versus mapped length choice, then emits spans by copying descriptors with adjusted first and last boundaries and terminating physical outputs.
Folio queue and xarray extraction treat missing queue linkage and unexpected value or huge page entries as warnings that stop emission without adding entries for the offending position.
Zero total size configuration for the sequential buffer is reported as a programming warning on append, format, hex, and path operations while still following overflow handling.

Kernel vector extraction derives page offset from the source address, splits each vector at page boundaries, and resolves backing pages through separate handling for virtual module addresses versus directly mapped addresses.
Folio queue extraction writes back the current queue reference together with slot index, intra folio offset, and remaining count into the iterator after consuming entries.
